questions.prompt: What can be concluded here about the letting of single sittings?

options.text: The boxes were divided mainly because more parishioners wanted seats than the church could hold.
Letting seats singly was the wardens' way of filling pews that would no longer let whole.
The single sittings were meant chiefly for poorer families, who had until then sat on the free benches.
After 1851 a whole box in the middle aisle could be had for two shillings a year.
